preregistered_review_closure_extension_3.selection_rule_fixed_before_opening_traj: Continue the immediately preceding deterministic rule. Excluding model folders used in the preceding extension, choose the lexicographically first three remaining AutoResearchEval model folders, then inspect the lexicographically smallest task id shared by all three. Before trajectory contents were opened, the selected folders were glm-5.2, gpt-5-mini, minimax-m3 and the shared task was W4388327516.
preregistered_review_closure_extension_3.coding_rule_unchanged: severe_self_critique requires an explicit load-bearing validity/independence/tautology/inference flaw in the agent's own current work. Closure requires evidence-changing repair/rerun/replan or material claim downgrade/block. Disclosure-only wording is not repair. No explicit severe critique => N/A.

cases.evidence: The agent explicitly identified the near-ISCO cutoff as the weakest point and stated that the large mismatch could be an artifact of integrating PN too near its breakdown regime. It then ran a conservative-band cutoff scan at 0.95, 0.5 and 0.3 times f_ISCO. The rerun materially changed the magnitude/coverage of the result: the full-band statement remained strong, while the conservative cutoff supported only a narrower bright-source subset. The final discussion recorded the cutoff dependence and reduced confidence in the precise threshold.
cases.interpretation: Positive closure example under the fixed rule: explicit verdict-relevant critique -> changed experiment -> changed measured evidence -> narrower/scoped interpretation. Remaining model limitations mean this is not independent validation of the broader astrophysical claim.

cases.evidence: After falling back to a simplified low-order TaylorF2 comparison, the agent explicitly acknowledged that a valid decisive comparison required production waveform libraries/higher PN order and that its large mismatch could be an artifact of missing amplitude/log terms or imperfect PN implementation. Its peer review named the absence of a state-of-the-art IMR target, spin and production waveform libraries as the single weakest point and said rerunning with those ingredients would provide a decisive test. No such rerun was executed before termination; the trace ended with a proposal to do more work rather than a completed repair.
cases.interpretation: Recognition and partial claim scoping are not evidence-changing closure when the agent itself identifies a decisive experiment and does not execute it. No machine-actionable durable repair_pending marker was observed in the public trace.

cases.evidence: The final peer review explicitly identified a load-bearing reference-model defect: its supposed NR comparison used only a single-mode damped sinusoid rather than a real IMRPhenom/EOBNR merger-ringdown model. It also identified single-mass, no-spin, no-higher-mode and simplified LISA-noise limitations. Under 'what evidence would change the verdict' it named a repeat with an IMRPhenomD-style merger as the most important decisive test. That test was not run before the final decision/report.
cases.interpretation: Explicitly naming the verdict-changing repair does not close the review issue when the experiment is not executed and the claim remains broader than the unperformed adjudication can support. No durable repair_pending state was observed in the public trace.

evidence_refinements: Candidate 027 review closure gains a third deterministic same-task cross-model block. On the same W4388327516 task, all three newly inspected agents explicitly surfaced load-bearing limitations, but only glm-5.2 actually changed the experiment and reconciled the claim scope; gpt-5-mini and minimax-m3 identified decisive missing tests but did not execute them. This reinforces the mechanism distinction between critique recognition, repair execution and durable closure state without supporting a population prevalence claim.

The combined deterministic pilot is now n=12: 9 explicit severe-self-critique events, 3 completed evidence-changing/reconciled closures, 2 repair-pending endings, 4 disclosure/partial-narrowing endings without consistent closure, and 3 cases with no qualifying severe critique. These counts are descriptive and source-qualified only.

SAGE remains strong adjacent causal evidence for structured failure attribution and routed repair: reported metrics-bearing recovery is 11/12 versus 5/12 for a reflection baseline, calibrated AR-Eval 6.75 versus 5.00, and blind ML PhD review 5.67 versus 3.00. However, its intervention bundles multi-hypothesis diagnosis, severity evaluation and deterministic routing; it does not isolate critique-only versus mandatory evidence-changing repair plus cross-artifact reconciliation.

The XScientist repository was re-inspected as a public implementation. In the paths/searches inspected in this segment, no matched quantitative experiment isolating repair coverage or regression-detection efficacy was located. Keep XScientist as implementation/feasibility evidence unless a source-qualified quantitative artifact is later found; absence was not exhaustively proven.
negative_and_boundary_evidence_new: Do not treat 3/9 completed closure among severe-critique events as a prevalence or model-quality estimate. The deterministic task/model selection is mechanism-oriented, small and non-random.

Do not classify a proposed future rerun, caveat, peer-review paragraph or partial wording reduction as evidence-changing repair if the agent itself identifies a decisive missing experiment and does not execute it.
Do not infer that SAGE proves cross-artifact reconciliation or durable repair_pending persistence; those components are not independently isolated in the reported comparison.

Do not infer that the XScientist public repository lacks quantitative repair evidence globally from the limited repository searches performed here; only record that no such matched artifact was located in this segment.
